Linked visualization examples

Source: vignettes/visualization-examples.Rmd
visualization-examples.Rmd

mosaic_gl() puts Mosaic views and GPU deck.gl layers in one browser scope over a single DuckDB-WASM coordinator and a single shared selection, so a brush in any panel filters every other panel.

Each example below is self-contained: it builds its own data, so you can paste it straight into the console. The last example keeps its data in a DuckDB database and draws polygons.

library(dbVisuals)
set.seed(1)

The three pieces

A spec is an ordinary R list shaped like a Mosaic spec, with two additions:

  • mgl_data() declares a data source — either an R data frame shipped as Arrow IPC (type = "table"), or a query left in DuckDB (type = "duckdb").
  • mgl_deckgl() declares a deck.gl panel as a Mosaic input, so it participates in the same selection as the Mosaic marks around it.

params = list(sel = list(select = "crossfilter")) creates the shared selection; panels write to it with a select clause and read from it with filterBy.

If you show several widgets on one page, give their tables different names: they share one DuckDB-WASM instance, so a reused name replaces the earlier table.

1. Cross-filtered scatter with a marginal histogram

A deck.gl scatterplot beside a Mosaic histogram. Brushing the histogram filters the points; the interval brush writes to $sel and the deck panel reads it.

cells <- data.frame(
  cell_ID    = sprintf("cell_%04d", 1:4000),
  x          = rnorm(4000, 0, 40),
  y          = rnorm(4000, 0, 40),
  total_expr = rpois(4000, 60)
)

spec1 <- mgl_spec(
  meta   = list(title = "Points cross-filtered by expression"),
  data   = list(cells1 = mgl_data(type = "table", df = cells)),
  params = list(sel = list(select = "crossfilter")),
  vconcat = list(
    list(
      plot = list(
        list(
          mark = "rectY",
          data = list(from = "cells1", filterBy = "$sel"),
          x    = list(bin = "total_expr"),
          y    = list(count = NULL),
          fill = "#60a5fa"
        ),
        list(
          select = "intervalX", as = "$sel",
          brush  = list(stroke = "currentColor", fill = "transparent")
        )
      ),
      width = 640, height = 110, marginLeft = 40
    ),
    mgl_deckgl(
      id        = "spatial",
      filter_by = "$sel",
      width     = 640, height = 420,
      layers = list(list(
        `@@type`         = "ScatterplotLayer",
        id               = "pts",
        data             = "cells1",
        getPosition      = "@@=[x, y]",
        getFillColor     = c(100L, 180L, 255L, 220L),
        getRadius        = 2,
        radiusUnits      = "pixels",
        coordinateSystem = "@@#COORDINATE_SYSTEM.CARTESIAN",
        positionFormat   = "XY",
        pickable         = TRUE
      ))
    )
  )
)

mosaic_gl(spec1, width = "100%", height = 560)

getPosition = "@@=[x, y]" and coordinateSystem = "@@#COORDINATE_SYSTEM.CARTESIAN" are the two conventions worth remembering: @@= marks a JavaScript accessor expression and @@# marks a deck.gl constant. Cartesian is what you want for tissue coordinates — the default is geographic.

2. Dimension-reduction pairs linked to a categorical bar

mgl_deckgl(concat = ...) lays out several panes that share one layer definition, each pane binding different columns to x and y. Toggling a bar in the Mosaic bar chart filters every pane at once.

dimred <- data.frame(
  cell_ID     = sprintf("cell_%04d", 1:2000),
  leiden_clus = sample(sprintf("c%02d", 1:8), 2000, replace = TRUE),
  umap_1 = rnorm(2000), umap_2 = rnorm(2000), umap_3 = rnorm(2000),
  pca_1  = rnorm(2000), pca_2  = rnorm(2000), pca_3  = rnorm(2000)
)

spec3 <- mgl_spec(
  meta   = list(title = "UMAP / PCA pairs linked to leiden_clus"),
  data   = list(dimred = mgl_data(type = "table", df = dimred)),
  params = list(sel = list(select = "crossfilter")),
  vconcat = list(
    list(
      plot = list(
        list(mark = "barY", data = list(from = "dimred", filterBy = "$sel"),
             x = "leiden_clus", y = list(count = NULL), fill = "#60a5fa"),
        list(select = "toggleX", as = "$sel")
      ),
      width = 700, height = 140, marginLeft = 40
    ),
    mgl_deckgl(
      id = "umap", filter_by = "$sel", width = 700, height = 210,
      concat = list(orient = "hconcat", panes = list(
        list(x = "umap_1", y = "umap_2", title = "UMAP 1 vs 2"),
        list(x = "umap_1", y = "umap_3", title = "UMAP 1 vs 3"),
        list(x = "umap_2", y = "umap_3", title = "UMAP 2 vs 3")
      )),
      layers = list(list(
        `@@type` = "ScatterplotLayer", id = "p", data = "dimred",
        getFillColor = c(100L, 180L, 255L, 220L),
        getRadius = 3, radiusUnits = "pixels", opacity = 0.85
      ))
    ),
    mgl_deckgl(
      id = "pca", filter_by = "$sel", width = 700, height = 210,
      concat = list(orient = "hconcat", panes = list(
        list(x = "pca_1", y = "pca_2", title = "PC 1 vs 2"),
        list(x = "pca_1", y = "pca_3", title = "PC 1 vs 3"),
        list(x = "pca_2", y = "pca_3", title = "PC 2 vs 3")
      )),
      layers = list(list(
        `@@type` = "ScatterplotLayer", id = "p", data = "dimred",
        getFillColor = c(245L, 158L, 11L, 220L),
        getRadius = 3, radiusUnits = "pixels", opacity = 0.85
      ))
    )
  )
)

mosaic_gl(spec3, width = "100%", height = 620)

3. Keeping data in DuckDB, and drawing polygons

The examples above ship their data frames to the browser. For anything large, leave the data in DuckDB and send only the query: mgl_data(type = "duckdb") with a con. Polygons travel as GeoArrow rather than JSON, and are drawn with GeoArrowPolygonLayer.

# A small spatial database, so this example runs anywhere. Substitute your own
# file and table names for real work.
db <- file.path(tempdir(), "cells.duckdb")
unlink(db)
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), db)
DBI::dbExecute(con, "INSTALL spatial")
DBI::dbExecute(con, "LOAD spatial")

DBI::dbExecute(con, "
  CREATE TABLE cell_polygons AS
  SELECT i AS cell_ID,
         ((i - 1) %  25) * 12.0 + 6 * random() AS x,
         ((i - 1) // 25) * 12.0 + 6 * random() AS y,
         CAST(20 + 60 * random() AS INTEGER)   AS total_expr
  FROM range(1, 501) t(i)")
DBI::dbExecute(con, "ALTER TABLE cell_polygons ADD COLUMN geom GEOMETRY")
DBI::dbExecute(con, "UPDATE cell_polygons SET geom = ST_Buffer(ST_Point(x, y), 4.5)")

spec4 <- mgl_spec(
  meta   = list(title = "Polygons and centroids from DuckDB"),
  data   = list(
    cells4 = mgl_data(
      type  = "duckdb",
      query = "SELECT cell_ID, x, y, total_expr FROM cell_polygons"
    ),
    polys4 = mgl_data(
      type   = "duckdb",
      # The key column matters: the WKB encoder needs a key (cell_ID /
      # poly_ID / id) alongside the geometry, or it falls back to plain
      # Arrow and the polygon layer is silently skipped.
      query  = "SELECT cell_ID, ST_AsWKB(geom) AS geometry FROM cell_polygons",
      format = "geoarrow"
    )
  ),
  params = list(sel = list(select = "crossfilter")),
  vconcat = list(
    list(
      plot = list(
        list(mark = "rectY", data = list(from = "cells4", filterBy = "$sel"),
             x = list(bin = "total_expr"), y = list(count = NULL), fill = "#a78bfa"),
        list(select = "intervalX", as = "$sel",
             brush = list(stroke = "currentColor", fill = "transparent"))
      ),
      width = 640, height = 110, marginLeft = 40
    ),
    mgl_deckgl(
      id = "insitu", filter_by = "$sel", width = 640, height = 440,
      layers = list(
        list(
          `@@type`           = "GeoArrowPolygonLayer",
          id                 = "polys",
          data               = "polys4",
          geometryColumn     = "geometry",
          getFillColor       = c(157L, 78L, 221L, 90L),
          stroked            = FALSE,
          lineWidthMinPixels = 0.4,
          coordinateSystem   = "@@#COORDINATE_SYSTEM.CARTESIAN",
          positionFormat     = "XY"
        ),
        list(
          `@@type`         = "ScatterplotLayer",
          id               = "centroids",
          data             = "cells4",
          getPosition      = "@@=[x, y]",
          getFillColor     = c(30L, 41L, 59L, 200L),
          getRadius        = 2,
          radiusUnits      = "pixels",
          coordinateSystem = "@@#COORDINATE_SYSTEM.CARTESIAN",
          positionFormat   = "XY"
        )
      )
    )
  )
)

mosaic_gl(spec4, con = con, width = "100%", height = 600)

Passing con also lets the widget issue follow-up queries against your R-side DuckDB as you interact, instead of materializing everything up front. Any spatial / nanoarrow / geoarrow extensions already loaded on that connection are reused.

In Shiny 

ui <- shiny::fluidPage(mosaic_glOutput("viewer", height = "780px"))

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$viewer <- renderMosaic_gl(mosaic_gl(spec1))
}

shiny::shinyApp(ui, server)
